request.description: I, Pencil: a pencil supply chain that keeps running. Loggers cut cedar in Oregon, a mill saws it into slats, graphite is mined in Sri Lanka and mixed with clay into leads, a factory in Pennsylvania glues leads into slats, paints them and adds erasers and brass ferrules, packs them into boxes, and trucks deliver the boxes to shops across the country, which sell them to customers.

second_source_processes: cedar-renewal adds stock.logs (already added from nothing by cut-cedar)
graphite-renewal adds stock.graphite (already added from nothing by mine-graphite)
raw-material-renewal adds stock.logs (already added from nothing by cut-cedar)
graphite-renewal adds stock.graphite (already added from nothing by mine-graphite)

world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: Specialists continually make, transport, and sell pencils.

actions.description: Cut cedar logs for the mill.
Saw logs into slats and pass them to the named recipient.
Mine graphite and pass it to the named recipient.
Pass clay to the named recipient.
Mix graphite and clay into leads for the named recipient.
Supply paint to the named recipient.
Supply erasers to the named recipient.
Supply brass ferrules to the named recipient.
Glue leads into slats, paint the pencils, and add erasers and ferrules.
Pack pencils into boxes.
Carry packed pencils from their source to a shop.
Sell pencils from the named shop to the named customer.

mechanics.rationale: Cutting cedar produces logs for the logger; no represented reserve supports a depletion effect.
limits: No tree reserve, tool, or logging cost is represented.
tests: A positive quantity adds that many logs to the logger.
Zero or negative quantity is refused.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the number of cedar logs cut

mechanics.rationale: The mill consumes source logs and transfers the resulting slats to the named recipient.

checks.label: the mill and log source are together
the mill and recipient are together

limits: One log yields one slat; no conversion ratio or processing loss is represented.
Cross-location delivery is not represented.
tests: Sufficient source logs are subtracted and equal slats are added to the recipient.
Insufficient stock or different locations are refused.

mechanics.rationale: Mining produces graphite and passes it to the named recipient; no reserve is represented to deplete.

checks.label: the miner and recipient are together

limits: No mine reserve is represented, so no depletion is modeled.
tests: A positive quantity adds graphite to the recipient.
A recipient in another location is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier transfers represented clay stock to a co-located recipient.

checks.label: the supplier and recipient are together

limits: No remote shipment or payment is described.
tests: Sufficient clay transfers from supplier to recipient.
Insufficient clay or different locations are refused.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker consumes graphite and clay from the named sources and delivers leads to the recipient.

checks.label: the graphite source has enough graphite
the clay source has enough clay
the maker and graphite source are together
the maker and clay source are together
the maker and recipient are together

limits: One unit of each ingredient is consumed per lead; no alternate recipe is represented.
tests: Sufficient co-located ingredients are consumed and leads are delivered.
Insufficient ingredients or a location mismatch is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier transfers represented paint stock to a co-located recipient.

checks.label: the supplier and recipient are together

limits: No remote shipment or payment is described.
tests: Sufficient paint transfers to the recipient.
Insufficient paint or different locations are refused.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier transfers represented eraser stock to a co-located recipient.

checks.label: the supplier and recipient are together

limits: No remote shipment or payment is described.
tests: Sufficient erasers transfer to the recipient.
Insufficient erasers or different locations are refused.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier transfers represented ferrule stock to a co-located recipient.

checks.label: the supplier and recipient are together

limits: No remote shipment or payment is described.
tests: Sufficient ferrules transfer to the recipient.
Insufficient ferrules or different locations are refused.

mechanics.rationale: Assembly consumes one unit of each named component for each pencil and adds finished pencils to the factory.

the lead source has enough leads

limits: One unit of each named input is consumed per pencil; no waste or production ratio is represented.
Inputs must be locally present; no incoming shipment is modeled here.
tests: Enough co-located inputs are consumed and pencils are added.
Any insufficient input or location mismatch is refused.
semantic_bindings: the five named sources provide assembly materials

mechanics.rationale: Packing consumes pencils and boxes and records the packed quantity in the factory inventory.
limits: One box packs one pencil; no box capacity is represented.
tests: Sufficient pencils and boxes become packed pencils.
Insufficient pencils or boxes are refused.

mechanics.rationale: The carrier starts a represented shipment and removes packed pencils from their source; arrival transfer cannot be represented with the available state.

checks.label: the source has enough packed pencils
the driver and source are together

limits: Destination inventory, carried quantity, arrival, and travel are not represented; this action does not deliver stock to the shop.
tests: With packed pencils and an idle driver at the source, a shipment starts.
An empty source or busy driver is refused.

mechanics.rationale: A sale transfers exactly one pencil and charges the represented price once.

checks.label: the customer can pay the price
the shop and customer are together
the acting shop is the named shop

limits: Each move sells exactly one pencil regardless of quantity; repeat for further sales.
No customer demand or order state is represented.
tests: A valid sale transfers one pencil and the exact price from customer to shop.
Insufficient stock, insufficient cash, or different locations are refused.
semantic_bindings: customer pays and receives the pencil

processes.rationale: Supplier inventories renew each round so finite starting stocks do not end supply activity.

checks.label: the supplier clay stock is nonnegative

processes.rationale: An active shipment takes time, so its represented round count decreases once per round; arrival transfer is not represented.
